## In brief

Studies of gender-affirming treatment measure many different things, in many different ways, so their results are hard to compare or combine. Together with transgender and gender diverse people, clinicians, researchers and policy-makers, we are agreeing on a short list of outcomes that every study of gender-affirming treatment for adults in Sweden should measure.

## Why it matters

Research on the outcomes of gender-affirming treatment has grown in recent years, but the evidence behind current recommendations is still weak. One reason is that studies choose different outcomes and measure them with different instruments. A core outcome set is an agreed minimum that every study reports, so that future studies can be compared and pooled.

## What we do

The work follows the recommendations of the Core Outcome Measures in Effectiveness Trials (COMET) initiative and runs in four phases.

1. We review the published research and international guidelines on gender-affirming treatment to list the outcomes already in use.
2. We ask transgender and gender diverse people which outcomes matter to them, through reports from patient and interest organisations and an anonymous survey.
3. Researchers, healthcare professionals, policy-makers and transgender and gender diverse adults rate each outcome by importance over two or three rounds of a Delphi survey.
4. A consensus meeting with representatives of every group agrees the final set.

## What we have found

## For researchers

- **Design:** core outcome set development following COMET guidance. Umbrella review, stakeholder survey, two to three Delphi rounds and a consensus meeting
- **Population:** transgender and gender diverse adults receiving gender-affirming treatment in Sweden
- **Analysis:** survey responses are analysed interpretively to identify candidate outcomes. Likert-type ratings are aggregated in each Delphi round to decide which outcomes advance
- **Ethics:** Swedish Ethical Review Authority, registration number 2024-04672-01
- **Registration:** COMET registration number 3223
- **Protocol:** Dahlén et al. (2025), *BMJ Open* 15(7):e098300. [doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2024-098300](https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjopen-2024-098300)
